messages.subject: model selection with rw2
parts:
Hi,
I want to compare multiple models with different covariates included as rw2 terms. Normally I would calculate posterior model probabilities based on ratios of marginal likelihoods (Bayes factors).
Is it OK to use the marginal likelihood returned automatically via results$mlik to compare models with rw2 components, or does the fact that "the term 0.5log(|R|*) of the normalisation constant is not computed..." makes such comparisons invalid?
I know that the prior and scaling (scale.model) will affect the marginal likelihood..but does leaving out the 0.5log(|R|*) from the normalisation constant affect the relative marginal likelihoods of different models?
If so, how can I compute that term, or where can I learn more about it?
Thanks
Jim

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] model selection with rw2
parts:
On Mon, 2014-09-15 at 23:28 -0700, Jim Thomson wrote:
>
> Hi,
> I want to compare multiple models with different covariates included
> as rw2 terms. Normally I would calculate posterior model probabilities
> based on ratios of marginal likelihoods (Bayes factors).
> Is it OK to use the marginal likelihood returned automatically via
> results$mlik to compare models with rw2 components, or does the fact
> that "the term 0.5log(|R|*) of the normalisation constant is not
> computed..." makes such comparisons invalid?
> I know that the prior and scaling (scale.model) will affect the
> marginal likelihood..but does leaving out the 0.5log(|R|*) from the
> normalisation constant affect the relative marginal likelihoods of
> different models?
> If so, how can I compute that term, or where can I learn more about
> it?

If you compare models with

y ~ f(, model="rw2")

against

y ~ f(, model="rw2") + f(, model="rw2")



using mlik, you'll need to include the term 0.5*log(|R|). yes


if the rw2 is defined on integers, then

INLA:::inla.rw(n, order = 1L, sparse = TRUE, scale.model = FALSE)

will compute the R, and scaled if scale.model=TRUE, and you can then
compute the missing term using


my.determinant = function(
A,
tol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps),
log=FALSE,
rankdef)
{
X = svd(A)
d = X$d
if (!missing(rankdef)) {
d = sort(X$d)[-(1:rankdef)]
} else {
d = X$d[X$d > max(tol * X$d[1L], 0.0)]
}
if (log) {
return (sum(log(d)))
} else {
return (prod(d))
}
}



The missing term is part of the normalizing constant for the RW2 term.


Let me know if this does not solve the problem
